league.name: Perennial Push for Penultimacy
notes: 2021 was a 14-team league with only 2 WR starter slots; 2022 onward is 12 teams with 3 WR slots.
ESPN did not retain preseason projections for 2023; proj column is 0 for most 2023 picks.
Superflex (ESPN lineup slot 7) has been active every season 2021-2025.

2021.name: I Wish I Had A Waller

rules.rule: The second quarterback is the best value on the board, and this room still underpays for it.
rules.why: QBs taken in rounds 7-9 returned 210.0 points against 157.3 for the RB/WR/TE taken alongside them (+52.7); in rounds 10-12 the gap is +62.3. Six of the ten biggest value picks in five seasons were QBs taken in rounds 6-12 - Mayfield rd 9 (365.8), Stafford rd 6 (350.4), Lawrence rd 8 (338.2), Nix rd 10 (317.2), Love rd 10 (319.1), Goff rd 12 (284.3).
rules.n: 170 QB picks vs 587 RB/WR/TE picks, 5 seasons

rules.rule: A quarterback who misses time is replaced by nothing. That is what makes them scarce here.
rules.why: ESPN projects every starting quarterback to play a full season, so its 24th-best QB for 2026 projects 239.1 points. Across five actual seasons the 24th-best QB scored 153.7. Twenty-four QBs start every week in a superflex league and there is no 25th worth having, so the real floor is 153.7 - and measuring against the projected floor instead quietly erases about 85 points of value from every quarterback.
rules.n: 5 seasons of realized outcomes vs ESPN preseason projections

rules.rule: ESPN's own board is built for a one-QB league. Do not draft from it here.
rules.why: Ranked inside the same 209-player pool, quarterbacks sit far later on ESPN than value over replacement says they belong. This board puts 15 quarterbacks inside the first three rounds; across five seasons the room itself has taken 13.4 by that point, so the market already knows. ESPN does not.
rules.n: 209 skill players, ESPN PPR order vs superflex VOR, same pool

rules.rule: Never spend a pick on a kicker or defense before round 13.
rules.why: K and D/ST were startable 85-100% of the time in every round band from 10 on. The 15 taken before round 13 averaged 133.1 points at position rank 6.6; the 125 taken from round 13 on averaged 118.5 at rank 7.7. One position rank of quality costs a skill player worth roughly 149 points.

rules.rule: Running back falls off a cliff after round 9. Take the backs you want before it.
rules.why: RB startable rate runs 85% in rounds 1-3 and 59% in 7-9, then collapses to 32% in 10-12 and 21% in 13-15. Wide receiver follows the same curve one band later. Tight end holds up best late.

rules.rule: Treat every projection as roughly 15% too high, and rank on the gaps rather than the totals.
rules.why: Across 933 picks with usable ESPN preseason projections, actual points came in at 0.82-0.90 of projection in every round band through 15. By position the ratio is 0.853 for QBs, 0.856 for RBs, 0.827 for WRs and 0.886 for TEs - this board deflates every projection by its own position's factor before ranking.

rules.rule: Your draft slot is not worth worrying about.
rules.why: Teams picking 1-4 averaged 6.75 wins and a 7.5 finish; slots 5-8 averaged 7.55 wins and 5.7; slots 9-14 averaged 6.73 wins and 6.9. The spread is inside the noise for 62 team-seasons.

rules.rule: The draft matters here. It is not all waivers.
rules.why: Total points from a team’s drafted players correlate +0.50 with wins and +0.64 with points scored. Rounds 1-3 supply only 26.3% of all drafted points, though - rounds 10-18 supply 36.6%. The draft is won in the middle and late rounds.
